promptLatex: A slip is drawn at random from a box holding the slips numbered 1 through 10, replaced, and the draw is repeated three times. Given that at least one of the three draws showed a slip numbered greater than 8, what is the probability that all three draws showed a slip numbered greater than 8?
hintLatex: Compute the probability of the condition and the probability of the stronger event, then take the ratio.
A slip greater than $8$ has probability $\frac{2}{10}$, so all three being greater than $8$ has probability $\frac{1}{125}$.
At least one being greater than $8$ is the complement of all three being at most $8$, namely $1 - (\frac{4}{5})^3 = \frac{61}{125}$.
solutionLatex:
A single draw is greater than $8$ with probability $\frac{2}{10} = \frac{1}{5}$, and the three draws are independent because the slip is replaced.

All three draws being greater than $8$ has probability $\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)^3 = \frac{1}{125}$. At least one draw being greater than $8$ is the complement of all three being at most $8$, so its probability is

1 - \left(\frac{4}{5}\right)^3 = 1 - \frac{64}{125} = \frac{61}{125}

Dividing gives $\frac{1/125}{61/125} = \frac{1}{61}$.
